original_object.title: Doubling conjecture for dimension-banned graphs
original_object.statement: Let a graph be **banned in dimension** $k$ when it has no orthogonal representation in dimension $k$. If a vertex of valence $k$ in a graph banned in dimension $k$ is doubled, then **the doubling conjecture.** the resulting graph is banned in dimension $k+1$. The paper presents this as a recursive construction of banned graphs; no proof or resolution is supplied.
original_object.source_name: Alberto Solís-Encina and José Ramón Portillo, “Orthogonal Representation of Graphs”, arXiv:1504.03662 (2015).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03662

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

original_object.title: Matching-deletion conjecture for critical graph dimension
original_object.statement:
Let $G$ be a critical graph (not banned), let $M$ be a maximal matching, and suppose that its orthogonal representation dimension satisfies $\rho ^\text{\perp}(G)=d$. **The matching-deletion conjecture.** The graph obtained by deleting the matching satisfies

$$
\rho ^\text{\perp}(G-M(G))\le d-1.
$$
 The source provides no proof or resolution.
original_object.source_name: Alberto Solís-Encina and José Ramón Portillo, “Orthogonal Representation of Graphs”, arXiv:1504.03662 (2015).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03662

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

original_object.title: Klostermeyer et al.'s odd-entry density conjecture for the Pascal rhombus
original_object.statement:
Let $G_n$ and $H_n$ be the numbers of odd and even entries, respectively, among the first $n$ rows of the Pascal rhombus. **Klostermeyer et al.'s odd-entry density conjecture.** Then

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{G_n}{H_n}=0.
$$

Thus odd entries become negligible relative to even entries in the initial rows as the number of rows tends to infinity; the source gives no resolution evidence.
original_object.source_name: Paul K. Stockmeyer, “The Pascal Rhombus and the Stealth Configuration”, arXiv:1504.04404 (2015).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04404

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

original_object.title: Ringle circle problem
original_object.statement: A tangent graph of a finite collection of circles in the plane has one vertex for each circle and an edge when two circles are tangent. Assume that no more than two circles pass through any point. **Ringle circle problem.** Tangent graphs for finite collections of circles in the plane satisfying this assumption have bounded chromatic numbers. The source gives no resolution status.
original_object.source_name: Gil Kalai, “Some old and new problems in combinatorial geometry I: Around Borsuk's problem”, arXiv:1505.04952 (2015).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04952

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

original_object.title: Large-depth value conjecture for the two-nut caching game
original_object.statement:
Assume the two-nut caching game with parameters $n$ and $h$, and let the value denote the optimal winning probability. **Large-depth value conjecture.** If

$$
\frac{n+1}{2}\le\frac{h^2}{\lfloor h\rfloor},
$$

then the value of the game is

$$
\frac{\lfloor h\rfloor}{n}.
$$

The source gives no proof or disproof.
original_object.source_name: Endre Csóka, “Limit theory of discrete mathematics problems”, arXiv:1505.06984 (2017).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06984

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

original_object.title: Haws' unimodular-subsimplex covering conjecture for matroid polytopes
original_object.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $P(M)$ be its matroid polytope. A **unimodular subsimplex** is a unimodular simplex contained in $P(M)$. **Haws' conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the polytope $P(M)$ is the union of its unimodular subsimplices. This is presented as a weaker conjecture than the regular unimodular triangulation conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
original_object.source_name: Benjamin Braun, “Unimodality Problems in Ehrhart Theory”, arXiv:1505.07377 (2017).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.07377

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

original_object.title: Bounded-row conjecture for three-pile Sharing Nim nim-sequences
original_object.statement:
For integers $a\geq 1$, consider the nim-sequence

$$
(\mathcal{G}(0,a,n))_{n\geq a}.
$$

**Bounded-row conjecture.** Given $a\geq 1$, the nim-sequence $(\mathcal{G}(0,a,n))_{n\geq a}$ is bounded.

The conjecture is based on computation and is presented as an open question about the distribution of nim-values in the rows of the table; no proof or resolution is given.
original_object.source_name: Nhan Bao Ho, “Three-pile Sharing Nim and the quadratic time winning strategy”, arXiv:1506.06961 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

original_object.title: Five-line Fano-flow conjecture
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **5-line Fano-flow** is a Fano-flow in which at most five lines of the Fano plane occur as flow values at vertices. **Five-line Fano-flow conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a 5-line Fano-flow. This is a relaxation of the four-line Fano-flow conjecture and is equivalent to the corresponding formulation using two 1-factors and a join.
original_object.source_name: Ligang Jin, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Eckhard Steffen, “Cores, joins and the Fano-flow conjectures”, arXiv:1601.05762 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05762

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2016). “As above, it was proved that $k<2$ and conjectured that either $k=0$ or $k=1$.”

original_object.title: Cyclic 1-weak core conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **1-weak core** is a weak core arising from three joins, with precisely one of the joins not a 1-factor; it is **cyclic** when it is a cycle. **Cyclic 1-weak core conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a cyclic 1-weak core. The paper proves that this is equivalent to the two 1-factors and a join conjecture.
original_object.source_name: Ligang Jin, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Eckhard Steffen, “Cores, joins and the Fano-flow conjectures”, arXiv:1601.05762 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05762

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2016). “As above, it was proved that $k<2$ and conjectured that either $k=0$ or $k=1$.”

original_object.title: Acyclic complement of two 1-factors conjecture
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph, and let $M_1,M_2$ be 1-factors of $G$. **Acyclic two-matchings conjecture.** There exist two 1-factors such that the complement of their union is acyclic. The paper identifies this as a stronger version of the three-1-factor acyclic-complement conjecture and explicitly disproves it.
original_object.source_name: Ligang Jin, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Eckhard Steffen, “Cores, joins and the Fano-flow conjectures”, arXiv:1601.05762 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05762

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2016). “As above, it was proved that $k<2$ and conjectured that either $k=0$ or $k=1$.”

original_object.title: The power-of-two conjecture for odd core partitions into distinct parts
original_object.statement:
Let $s$ be odd, and consider $(s,s+2)$-core partitions into distinct parts. **Power-of-two conjecture.** Their number equals

$$
2^{s-1}.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed extension beyond the cases it proves, seeking a general enumeration of $(s,t)$-core partitions into distinct parts for coprime $s$ and $t$.
original_object.source_name: Armin Straub, “Core partitions into distinct parts and an analog of Euler's theorem”, arXiv:1601.07161 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.07161

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

original_object.title: The quadratic growth-ratio conjecture for van der Waerden numbers in the progression length
original_object.statement:
Let $W(r,k)$ denote the van der Waerden number. **Quadratic growth-ratio conjecture.** As $k$ grows large with $k>r$,

$$
\frac{W(r,k+1)}{W(r,k)}<k(k+1).
$$

This is the simplified form obtained in the source under the additional assumption that $m_{k+1}-m_k\in[0,1]$; the source gives no resolution.
original_object.source_name: Robert J Betts, “Two Upper Bounds for both the van der Waerden Numbers W(r, k + 1) and W(r + 1, k), that show the Existence of a Recurrence Relation”, arXiv:1603.01831 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01831

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

original_object.title: Monotonicity and CM-monotonicity for valuations
original_object.statement:
Let $d719$ be a $d4aa$-valuation for any $d4aa$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** $d719$ is monotone if and only if $d719$ is CM-monotone.

This conjecture asks whether the equivalence between monotonicity and CM-monotonicity, proved in the paper for $d719$ an $d4d9^d$-valuation, holds for valuations over any coefficient structure $d4aa$.
original_object.source_name: Katharina Jochemko and Raman Sanyal, “Combinatorial mixed valuations”, arXiv:1605.07431 (2017).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.07431

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

original_object.title: Lehel's cycle partition conjecture
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\overline G$ denote its complement. **Lehel's conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be covered by a cycle $C_1$ in $G$ and a vertex-disjoint cycle $C_2$ in $\overline G$. This is a two-colour cycle-partition problem for complete graphs and is presented as a motivation for studying sparse complements of cycles; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
original_object.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Partitioning a graph into a cycle and a sparse graph”, arXiv:1607.03348 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

original_object.title: Turan's conjecture on graph-property sensitivity
original_object.statement:
Let $f$ be a non-trivial graph property for graphs with $n$ vertices, so that $f$ is a Boolean function of the ${n \choose 2}$ possible edges. **Turan's conjecture.** The sensitivity satisfies

$$
s(f)\geq n-1.
$$

Turan had previously proved the lower bound $s(f)\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor$; the conjecture remains unresolved more than thirty years after it was formulated.
original_object.source_name: Ilan Karpas, “Lower bounds for sensitivity of graph properties”, arXiv:1609.05320 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05320

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2016).

original_object.title: Optimality of the B-E Construction for PIR array codes
original_object.statement: Let $s>2$, and consider the PIR array codes produced by the B-E Construction. **B-E optimality conjecture.** These PIR array codes have optimal rate. The preceding discussion is based on intuitive rather than strict proofs and gives positive evidence for the conjecture; proving or disproving the optimality of the B-E Construction remains of great interest.
original_object.source_name: Yiwei Zhang, Xin Wang, Hengjia Wei and Gennian Ge, “On private information retrieval array codes”, arXiv:1609.09167 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

original_object.title: The dichromatic Mader bound for oriented cycles
original_object.statement: Let $C$ be an oriented cycle, and let $\vec\chi(D)$ be the dichromatic number of a digraph $D$. **Dichromatic-cycle conjecture.** Every oriented cycle $C$ satisfies $\operatorname{mader}_{\vec\chi}(C)\leq |C|$. The surrounding text gives a weaker established bound for oriented cycles, so this stronger inequality is presented as an open conjecture.
original_object.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Nathann Cohen, Fréderic Havet, William Lochet, Phablo F. S. Moura and Stéphan Thomassé, “Subdivisions in digraphs of large out-degree or large dichromatic number”, arXiv:1610.00876 (2016).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00876

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2016). “Mader proved that $\mad_{\delta^+}(TT_4) = 3$, but even the existence of $\mad_{\delta^+}(TT_5)$ is still open.”

original_object.title: The triangle-freeness conjecture for Cheeger graphs
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a Cheeger graph, meaning a graph attaining the first Cheeger constant of the relevant simplex. **Triangle-freeness conjecture.** All Cheeger graphs are triangle-free. This is motivated by the authors' examples, in which an optimal graph's Cheeger constant receives no contribution from a triangle whose three edges all belong to the graph. The conjecture is presented as an open problem.
original_object.source_name: D. N. Kozlov, “The first Cheeger constant of a simplex”, arXiv:1610.07136 (2017).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07136

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2016). “We finish this section with two open problems, which are probably rather hard, but which might help to stimulate further research.”

original_object.title: The bipartiteness conjecture for Cheeger graphs
original_object.statement: Let $G$ be a Cheeger graph, meaning a graph attaining the first Cheeger constant of the relevant simplex. **Bipartiteness conjecture.** All Cheeger graphs are bipartite. This is proposed as a stronger statement than the conjecture that all Cheeger graphs are triangle-free. It is presented as an open problem.
original_object.source_name: D. N. Kozlov, “The first Cheeger constant of a simplex”, arXiv:1610.07136 (2017).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07136

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2016). “We finish this section with two open problems, which are probably rather hard, but which might help to stimulate further research.”

original_object.title: The conjecture that all difference sets are Desarguesian
original_object.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a difference set of order $q$, and let $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{D})$ be the generalized triangle constructed from it. The difference set $\mathcal{D}$ is **Desarguesian** if $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{D})\cong\mathcal{T}(q)$. **Desarguesian difference set conjecture.** Every difference set is Desarguesian.
original_object.source_name: William Norledge, “Singer cyclic lattices of type M”, arXiv:1711.09332 (2020).
original_object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09332

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).
